mainTopic: Building the fires on the מזבח, and the גמרא's discussion of exaggerated language in the תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים.
overview: The משנה finishes describing the ash heap and says the כהן was never lazy about clearing the ashes. It then explains how the fire on the מזבח was built. Every kind of wood is allowed except vine and olive, but fig, nut and pine were the usual choices. The large מערכה sat on the east side, and a second, smaller מערכה of fine fig wood was built near the southwest corner for the קטורת coals. On שבת that second fire was larger, because the בזיכי לבונה of the לחם הפנים were burned there. Leftover limbs and fats were put back on the fire, both fires were lit, and the כהנים went to לשכת הגזית. The גמרא then quotes רבא, who says the משנה's 300 כור of ashes and the golden cup for the תמיד are exaggerations. רבי אמי adds that the תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים all sometimes speak this way. שמואל limits the חכמים' exaggerations to three cases (the ash heap, the vine and the פרכת) and holds that the golden cup was real, because there is no poverty in a place of wealth. The גמרא begins describing the golden vine, and that description continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The כהן was never lazy about removing the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its description of the ash heap by stating that the כהן never slacked off about removing the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן was never lazy about taking out the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is wrapping up the topic of the ash heap on the מזבח by praising the כהנים: they always took the ashes out and never got lazy about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה described the ashes being piled into a heap in the middle of the מזבח. This line adds that the כהן never let that heap get neglected. It closes the ash topic before the משנה moves on to building the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: priest serving in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The kohen was never lazy
about taking out the ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִתְעַצֵּל הַכֹּהֵן מִלְּהוֹצִיא אֶת הַדֶּשֶׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה's earlier discussion of the ash heap, which came before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן always removed the ashes and never neglected it.

steps.title: The כהנים begin bringing up logs to build the wood pile
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new stage of the morning service: carrying logs up onto the מזבח to build the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They started bringing up logs to set up the wood pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next job: the כהנים start carrying logs up to the מזבח to build the wood pile. This sets up the next question about which wood may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ashes taken care of, the top of the מזבח is ready for a new fire. The משנה names the action, bringing up logs, and its purpose, setting up the מערכה. Mentioning the logs leads straight into the question of which trees are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the arranged wood pile on the מזבח where the fire burns

phrases.english: They began bringing up the logs
to set up the wood pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בַּגְּזִירִין לְסַדֵּר אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ash removal to the next stage, building the fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the ashes were handled, the כהנים brought logs up to build the מערכה.

steps.title: Is every kind of wood allowed for the pile?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה stops to ask whether wood from any tree may be used for the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is wood from every tree fit for the wood pile?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a simple clarifying question: may the logs come from any kind of tree? It is setting up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 just said logs were brought up but did not say what kind. This question fills that gap. It is a real request for information, not an attack on anything.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it so that...? (opens a question)

phrases.english: And is wood from all the trees
fit for the wood pile?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כׇּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִין לַמַּעֲרָכָה הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the logs mentioned in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kinds of wood may be used for the מערכה.

steps.title: All wood is allowed except vine and olive, but certain woods were usual
steps.stepSummary: The משנה answers that any wood is allowed except vine and olive wood, and lists the woods the כהנים usually used: young fig branches, nut wood and pinewood.
steps.simpleTranslation: All wood is fit for the pile except vine and olive wood. But these were the usual ones: young branches of fig, nut, and pinewood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question: every tree is allowed except grapevine and olive. Then it tells us which woods the כהנים actually used most of the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer has two parts. First comes the law: only vine and olive are left out. Second comes the usual practice: fig, nut and pine were the regular choice. The משנה does not give a reason for leaving out vine and olive here.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think fig, nut and pine were the only woods allowed. Every wood except vine and olive was fit. Those three were just the ones the כהנים usually used.

phrases.english: Wood from all the trees is fit for the wood pile
except for vine and olive wood.
But these were the ones they usually used:
young branches of the fig tree,
of the nut tree, and of pinewood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִין לַמַּעֲרָכָה חוּץ מִשֶּׁל גֶּפֶן וְשֶׁל זַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All wood is fit except vine and olive; the usual woods were young fig branches, nut wood and pinewood.
steps.whatToRemember: Allowed: every wood except vine and olive. Usual practice: fig, nut, pine.

steps.title: How the large wood pile was built on the east side
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the big מערכה: it sat on the east side of the מזבח, its open front faced east, the inner ends of the logs touched the ash heap, and gaps were left between logs for lighting kindling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He set up the large wood pile on the east side, with its front facing east. The inner ends of the logs touched the ash heap. There was space between the logs, because they would light the kindling from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the shape and position of the main wood pile on the מזבח, step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large מערכה was on the east side with its opening toward the east. The logs reached inward until they touched the תפוח in the middle of the מזבח. Gaps were left between the logs so the kindling could be lit there.

keyTerms.meaning: the large wood pile, the main fire
the round ash heap in the middle of the מזבח
kindling, small twigs used to start the fire

phrases.english: He set up the large wood pile on the east side,
and its front faced east.
And the inner ends of the logs
would touch the ash heap.
And there was space between the logs,
because they would light the kindling from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the building of the מערכה begun in step 2, after the side question about wood types.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The large מערכה was built on the east side, opening east, logs touching the תפוח, with gaps for lighting the kindling.

steps.title: The second wood pile for the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים picked out fine fig wood and built a second מערכה for the קטורת near the southwest corner of the מזבח, four אמות north of the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: They picked out nice fig wood from there. He set up the second wood pile for the קטורת, across from the southwest corner, pulled in from the corner toward the north four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes a second, separate wood pile: what wood it was made of and exactly where it stood on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pile used fine fig logs selected from the wood brought up. Its job was the קטורת, the incense. Its position is given carefully: near the southwest corner, measured four אמות toward the north.
steps.whatToRemember: There were two piles: the large מערכה on the east side, and a second מערכה of fine fig wood for the קטורת near the southwest corner, four אמות toward the north.

phrases.english: They picked out from there nice fig logs,
phrases.notes: "From there" means from the wood that was brought up to the מזבח.

phrases.english: he set up the second wood pile for the incense
across from the southwest corner,

phrases.aramaic: מָשׁוּךְ מִן הַקֶּרֶן כְּלַפֵּי צָפוֹן אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: pulled in from the corner toward the north four amos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the large מערכה, the משנה goes on to the second מערכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second מערכה of fine fig wood was built for the קטורת near the southwest corner, four אמות toward the north.

steps.title: How big the second fire was, on weekdays and on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The קטורת fire was built with enough wood to make five סאין of coals, and eight סאין on שבת, because the לבונה of the לחם הפנים was burned there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second fire was sized to give about five סאין of coals. On שבת it was sized to give about eight סאין of coals, because that is where they put the two בזיכי לבונה of the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps describing the second מערכה from the last step and tells us how much wood went into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount is measured by the coals the wood would produce, not by the wood itself. On שבת the fire had to be bigger because there was more to burn: the two בזיכי לבונה taken off the שולחן with the old לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The two small cups of frankincense set beside the showbread
The showbread on the שולחן, replaced every שבת

phrases.english: Estimated to produce five se'a of coals.
And on Shabbat, estimated to produce eight se'a of coals.
For there they would place

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
phrases.english: The two bowls of frankincense of the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes describing the second מערכה introduced in step 6 by giving its size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת מערכה holds enough wood for 5 סאין of coals on weekdays and 8 on שבת, because of the בזיכי לבונה.

steps.title: Returning leftovers, lighting both fires, and going down
steps.stepSummary: Limbs and fats not fully burned overnight are put back on the big מערכה. Both fires are lit, and the כהנים go down to לשכת הגזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Limbs and fats that had not burned up since the evening are put back onto the fire. They lit the two fires, came down, and went to לשכת הגזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes this stage of the service. The leftovers go back on, the fires are lit, and the כהנים leave for the next stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pieces of offerings that did not finish burning during the night are not thrown away. They go back onto the fire so they can burn completely. Going down to לשכת הגזית sets up the next stage, where they will hold the next lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chamber of Hewn Stone in the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The morning מזבח stage ends with two lit fires (the big one and the קטורת one), the leftover pieces back on the fire, and the כהנים going to לשכת הגזית.

phrases.english: The limbs and the fats
That were not consumed since the evening,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is printed in the standard גמרא, but the corrected text leaves it out.

phrases.english: They return them to the arrangement,
And they kindled the two arrangements with fire.
They went down and came to the Chamber of Hewn Stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the building of the מערכות described in steps 5-7 and closes this part of the service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover limbs and fats go back on the מערכה, both מערכות are lit, and the כהנים go to לשכת הגזית.

steps.title: רבא: some descriptions in the משנה are exaggerations
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה's claim of 300 כור of ashes is an exaggeration. He says the same about watering the תמיד from a golden cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. רבא said: that is an exaggeration. 'They gave the תמיד lamb water from a gold cup.' רבא said: that is an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by telling us not to read certain lines in the משנה literally. רבא labels them as exaggerations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the ash pile sometimes reached 300 כור, and a later משנה says the lamb drank from a gold cup. רבא explains that these are ways of saying 'a huge amount' or 'very fancy', not exact facts.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the משנה is wrong or that these practices never happened. He is saying the wording is exaggerated for emphasis.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rava said: It is an exaggeration.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's earlier line that the ash pile in the middle of the מזבח sometimes reached 300 כור.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁקוּ אֶת הַתָּמִיד בְּכוֹס שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: 'They gave the daily offering to drink from a cup of gold,'
phrases.notes: This line comes from a later משנה in this מסכת.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is an exaggeration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and goes back to an earlier line of the משנה (300 כור of ashes) to explain its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 300 כור of ashes and the golden cup for the תמיד are exaggerated expressions.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים all use exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי widens רבא's point: the תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים all sometimes speak in exaggerated language.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: the תורה spoke in exaggerated language, the נביאים spoke in exaggerated language, and the חכמים spoke in exaggerated language.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי makes a general rule that fits רבא's comments. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא brings an example for each of the three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's comments could look like a special excuse for the משנה. רבי אמי shows this is a normal way of speaking across all levels of holy texts, so overstatement is an accepted style.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a lasting reading rule: not every number or description in holy texts is meant literally.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
The Torah spoke exaggerated language,
The prophets spoke exaggerated language,
The sages spoke exaggerated language.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה לְשׁוֹן הֲבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבא's specific comments into a general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים all sometimes use exaggerated language.

steps.title: The תורה's example: cities walled up to the heavens
steps.stepSummary: The proof that the תורה exaggerates is the פסוק saying the cities were fortified 'in the heavens'. That obviously cannot be literal, so it is an exaggeration.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The תורה spoke in exaggerated language,' as it says: 'cities great and fortified up to the heavens.' Could you really think they reached the heavens? Rather, it is an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings its first example for רבי אמי, the one from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא asks whether anyone could take 'in the heavens' literally, and the answer is plainly no. So the פסוק is using an exaggeration to describe very tall walls, which proves the תורה uses such language.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (asked when the answer is obviously no)

phrases.english: 'The Torah spoke exaggerated language':
As it is written:
"Cities great and fortified up to the heavens"
In the heavens, would it enter your mind?!
Rather, it is an exaggeration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of three examples supporting רבי אמי's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's claim that the תורה uses exaggerated language
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 9:1, 'cities great and fortified in the heavens', which cannot be literal

steps.title: Proof that the חכמים exaggerate
steps.stepSummary: The examples of the חכמים exaggerating are the ash heap (תפוח) and watering the תמיד from a golden cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים spoke in exaggerated language, as we said: the ash heap, and 'they gave the תמיד water to drink from a cup of gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps proving רבי אמי's claim. Now it shows that the חכמים also exaggerate, using the two examples רבא already gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the גמרא proved the תורה exaggerates. Here it points back to step 9, where רבא called the 300 כור ash heap and the golden cup exaggerations. Those two lines in the משנה are the proof for the חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: This line lists the golden cup as an exaggeration, following רבא. In a moment שמואל will disagree and say the golden cup was real. Don't assume this example is the final word.

phrases.english: The Sages spoke exaggerated language:
this that we said: the ash heap,
phrases.notes: He means the 300 כור heap of ashes that רבא called an exaggeration in step 9.

phrases.english: and 'they gave the תמיד water to drink'
'from a cup of gold.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second of three proofs for רבי אמי's claim; step 11 covered the תורה, this covers the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's claim that the חכמים sometimes speak in exaggeration
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's descriptions of the ash heap and the golden cup, which רבא called exaggerations

steps.title: Proof that the נביאים exaggerate
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים exaggerate: the פסוק says the earth split from the sound of the people's music.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נביאים spoke in exaggerated language, as it is written: 'the people piped with pipes, and the earth split from their sound.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last proof for רבי אמי: the נביאים also exaggerate. The פסוק about the earth splitting from the music cannot be literal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like 'fortified in the heavens' in step 11, the earth did not really crack open. The פסוק means the sound was extremely loud. This completes all three parts of רבי אמי's claim: תורה, נביאים and חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's rule is now fully proven: the תורה, the נביאים and the חכמים all sometimes speak in exaggerated language.

phrases.english: The prophets spoke exaggerated language,
as it is written: "(And all the people of the land)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The actual פסוק opens with 'And all the people came up after him.'

phrases.english: piped with pipes, etc.
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:40, at the crowning of שלמה.

phrases.english: and the earth split from their sound."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final proof for רבי אמי's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's claim that the נביאים sometimes speak in exaggeration
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 1:40, the earth splitting from the sound of the music

steps.title: שמואל: the חכמים exaggerated in only three places
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the חכמים used exaggerated language in exactly three places: the ash heap, the vine and the פרכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: In three places the חכמים spoke in exaggerated language. They are: the ash heap, the vine and the פרכת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: שמואל gives a fixed list of the only three places where the חכמים exaggerated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave two examples, the ash heap and the golden cup. שמואל agrees about the ash heap, but his list of three does not include the golden cup. Instead it adds the vine and the פרכת.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden vine at the entrance of the היכל
The curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי בַּר נַחְמָנִי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai bar Nachmani said that Shmuel said:
In three places
the Sages spoke in exaggerated language,
and these are they:
the ash heap, the vine, and the curtain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי בַּר נַחְמָנִי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a limited list that differs from רבא's examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים exaggerated in only three places: the ash heap, the vine and the פרכת.

steps.title: שמואל's list rejects רבא about the golden cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל's list comes to reject רבא: the three listed cases are exaggerations, but the golden cup is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to exclude רבא's view. We learned: 'They gave the תמיד water from a cup of gold,' and רבא said it is an exaggeration. שמואל teaches us: these three are exaggerations, but that one is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל bothered to give an exact count of three. The point is to reject רבא's claim that the golden cup was an exaggeration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'only three' and leaving out the golden cup, שמואל is telling us the golden cup was literally true. So רבא and שמואל disagree about the golden cup. They agree about the ash heap.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject a different view

phrases.english: This comes to exclude Rava's view,
for we learned: 'They gave the תמיד water to drink
from a cup of gold,'
and Rava said: It is an exaggeration.
Shmuel teaches us:
these, yes; there, no.
phrases.notes: 'These' are the three cases on שמואל's list. 'There' is the golden cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of שמואל's exact count in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבא's claim about the golden cup, not his claim about the ash heap
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא treated the golden cup as an exaggeration, but שמואל's closed list of three leaves it out, so it was literally true.

steps.title: No poverty in a place of wealth
steps.stepSummary: The reason the golden cup was real: in the rich setting of the בית המקדש, they do not use cheap items.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason why the golden cup could really have been gold. The בית המקדש is a place of wealth, so even a simple cup was made of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא called the golden cup an exaggeration, but the גמרא never says why. This principle explains why the cup could really have been gold. In the בית המקדש everything is done in a rich and honorable way, so a golden cup makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Poverty, acting in a cheap way
Wealth, a rich and honorable setting

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the חכמים exaggerated only about the ash heap, the vine and the פרכת. The golden cup was real, because there is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אין עניות במקום עשירות is a well-known rule about the honor of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: There is no poverty in a place of wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind rejecting רבא in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The golden cup for the תמיד was literally gold, because the בית המקדש is a place of wealth where nothing is done cheaply.

steps.title: The ash heap is the case we already discussed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts going through שמואל's three cases. The first, the תפוח (ash heap), is the one already discussed earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ash heap: that is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining which sources שמואל meant in his list of three exaggerations. For the first one, the תפוח, it simply points back to what was already discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave only short labels: ash heap, vine, פרכת. The גמרא now matches each label to its actual source. The ash heap needs no new quote, because רבא already called it an exaggeration (step 9), and the גמרא listed it again as the חכמים' example (step 12).

keyTerms.meaning: "That which we said": pointing back to an earlier discussion

phrases.english: The ash heap: that is what we already said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the conclusion about the golden cup back to explaining each item in שמואל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'ash heap' in שמואל's list is the same ash heap exaggeration discussed earlier.

steps.title: The source for the golden vine
steps.stepSummary: For the second case, the גפן (vine), the גמרא begins quoting a teaching: a golden vine stood at the entrance of the היכל, spread over posts, and people could donate gold pieces to add to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vine: as it was taught: A golden vine stood at the entrance of the היכל, and it was spread out over posts. And anyone who would donate a leaf...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now identifies the second exaggeration, the vine, by starting to quote the teaching that describes it. The quote continues past this point, and the exaggerated part is still coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the ash heap, the vine was not discussed yet, so the גמרא brings its source. So far the description is simple: a golden vine on posts at the היכל entrance, which grew through people's gold donations. The over-the-top detail that makes it an exaggeration comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A golden vine, an ornament made in the shape of a grapevine
The entrance to the היכל, the main building of the בית המקדש
Spread out or hung, the way a vine is trained over supports
Someone who donates by his own free will
A leaf, here a golden leaf added to the vine

phrases.english: The vine: as it was taught:
